title.en: One boat, more than 400 people and 25 years of consequences
title.zh: 一艘船，400多人和25年的后果

summary.en: Twenty-five years after the Tampa affair, the people, policies, and political fault lines behind Australia's border debate remain.
summary.zh: 坦帕事件25年后，澳大利亚边境辩论背后的人物、政策和政治分歧依然存在。

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

For Farid — a pseudonym used to protect his identity — those three words still carry him back 25 years, to a ship in the Indian Ocean, a teenage boy surrounded by hundreds of strangers, and the sudden arrival of Australian authorities after the vessel that had rescued him was prevented from reaching Christmas Island — an Australian territory.

He was 17. He had fled Afghanistan, leaving behind his single mother and siblings, and spent eight months moving from one boat to another in search of safety.

By the time the Norwegian freighter MV Tampa rescued him and 432 other asylum seekers — most of them Hazara Afghans — from a stricken fishing boat named the Palapa in August 2001, he had already endured storms, days at sea and the uncertainty of not knowing where the journey would end. At the time, Hazaras were fleeing Afghanistan, fearing persecution from the resurgent Taliban.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"We weren't clearly told where they were going to take us. When we first saw the authorities' ship, I thought they were going to take us to Australia," Farid tells SBS News.

Instead, he was taken to Nauru , where he would spend years caught up in Australia's newly established offshore processing system before eventually returning to Afghanistan.

"It was like a camp. We get our turns, about once a month, to go out for a few hours," he says.

"For the first year we didn't get to go out at all. We were not very hopeful. It was just tents at first, but then they set up portable rooms," Farid says.

Today, he is 42 and lives in Melbourne's south-east, where he works as a painter after completing trade courses and an apprenticeship. He was granted asylum in Australia in 2012.

The ordinary life Farid has built in Australia is a long way from the journey that brought him here, one that began when he was a teenager fleeing Afghanistan and led him into the centre of the 'Tampa crisis' and Australia's emerging offshore processing system .

Twenty-five years on, his experience offers a human window into the events surrounding the Tampa and the policy that followed, known as the Pacific Solution, as Australia continues to debate how it responds to people seeking protection.

On 24 August 2001, the Palapa ran into trouble in rough seas about 140km north of Christmas Island, leaving those on board facing the prospect of sinking.

Two days later, on 26 August, Australia's Rescue Coordination Centre alerted ships in the area that the vessel was in distress, with the words "HELP" and "SOS" painted across its roof.

The closest...
body.zh: 分享您的反馈并帮助我们改进此功能。请在此处详细了解我们如何在 SBS 使用人工智能。 对于法里德（Farid）——一个用来保护自己身份的化名——来说，这三个词仍然把他带回到 25 年前，印度洋上的一艘船上，一个十几岁的男孩被数百名陌生人包围，以及在营救他的船只无法到达澳大利亚领土圣诞岛后，澳大利亚当局突然赶到。 他当时 17 岁。他离开了阿富汗，留下了单亲母亲和兄弟姐妹，花了八个月的时间从一艘船搬到另一艘船以寻求安全。 2001 年 8 月，当挪威货船 MV Tampa 从一艘名为 Palapa 的失事渔船上救出他和其他 432 名寻求庇护者（其中大多数是哈扎拉阿富汗人）时，他已经经历了暴风雨、在海上漂泊的日子以及不知道旅程将在哪里结束的不确定性。当时，哈扎拉人因担心受到死灰复燃的塔利班的迫害而逃离阿富汗。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 法里德告诉 SBS 新闻：“我们没有明确告知他们要带我们去哪里。当我们第一次看到当局的船时，我以为他们会带我们去澳大利亚。” 相反，他被带到瑙鲁，在那里他在澳大利亚新建立的离岸加工系统中度过了数年，然后最终返回阿富汗。 “这就像一个营地。我们大约每月一次轮流出去几个小时，”他说。 “第一年，我们根本不能出去。我们没有太大希望。一开始只是帐篷，但后来他们设立了便携式房间，”法里德说。 如今，他 42 岁，住在墨尔本东南部，完成贸易课程和学徒期后，他在那里担任画家。 2012年，他在澳大利亚获得庇护。 法里德在澳大利亚建立的平凡生活与他来到这里的旅程相去甚远，他十几岁的时候就开始了逃离阿富汗的旅程，并带领他进入了“坦帕危机”和澳大利亚新兴离岸加工系统的中心。 二十五年过去了，他的经历为了解坦帕事件及其随后的政策（称为“太平洋解决方案”）提供了一个人性化的窗口，澳大利亚仍在争论如何应对寻求保护的人。 2001年8月24日，帕拉帕号在圣诞岛以北约140公里处的波涛汹涌的海面上遇到麻烦，船上的人面临沉没的危险。 两天后，即 8 月 26 日，澳大利亚救援协调中心向该地区的船只发出该船遇险的警报，并在船顶涂上了“HELP”和“SOS”字样。 最近的...

reflection.en: The story of Farid, who fled Afghanistan at 17 and found himself caught in Australia's border policies, echoes the long-term human impact of such decisions. For 25 years, the debate has continued, leaving individuals like Farid in prolonged uncertainty. The ancient call to welcome the foreigner, to treat the stranger as one of your own, remains a profound...
reflection.zh: 法里德的故事，他17岁时逃离阿富汗，却发现自己陷入澳大利亚的边境政策之中，这呼应了此类决定长期的个人影响。25年来，争论仍在继续，让像法里德这样的人长期处于不确定之中。古老的呼召——要欢迎外国人，待客如本地人——仍然是对那些在边境管制中挣扎的国家一个深刻的挑战。

verse.textEn: And you are to love those who are foreigners, for you yourselves were foreigners in Egypt.
verse.textZh: 所以你们要怜爱寄居的，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

title.en: Neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell has been talking about autism. Experts say he's recruiting
title.zh: 新纳粹分子托马斯·塞维尔谈论自闭症。专家称他正在招募

summary.en: Neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell has been recorded joking about 'recruiting' autistic men and discussing how to channel their 'fixations.' Experts warn this is a tactic to recruit vulnerable individuals into extremist movements.
summary.zh: 新纳粹分子托马斯·塞维尔被录下视频，他开玩笑地谈论“招募”自闭症男性并讨论如何引导他们的“执念”。专家警告说，这是将弱势个体招募到极端主义运动中的一种策略。

body.en:
Watch the full documentary 'Autism, Extremism and Recruitment' on our YouTube channel.

"Adolf Hitler, huge autist, massive autist, like all these incredible men, some of the best men that ever lived," Thomas Sewell tells viewers online.

Sewell, a neo-Nazi who led the National Socialist Network (NSN), now White Australia, is 10 minutes into a 22-minute monologue giving his "take" on autism.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"We used to bully nerds and now we coddle them. Now we're like, 'Oh, you have a disability. You're autistic.' And we treat them like that they're f---ing retarded."

Sewell repeatedly returns to the idea that autistic men do not need to be treated differently, but instead need challenge, male role models and to ‘channel their fixations’. He suggests joining the military — Sewell is ex-Army himself — learning a trade or pursuing higher education.

Running through his commentary is Sewell’s own movement. He tells viewers about one former NSN member he says he took under his wing.

"I became like his big brother, and I taught him how to lift [weights], and I taught him how to fight and I taught him how to talk to girls and after two years of just intense bullying … he became like a normal person."

A year later, in 2025, Sewell shared another video speaking about autism. This time he was criticising a Countering Violent Extremism program.

"I've recruited hundreds of autistic teenagers and zero of them have stabbed anyone," Sewell jokes.

We contacted Sewell and he denied that he ever actively recruited autistic people.

But his comments come as the Australian Federal Police (AFP) and researchers stress that extremist groups target young people, who they see as vulnerable, including those who are neurodivergent.

Peta Lowe, who spent years leading the NSW government’s countering violent extremism program for young people, has no doubts about the video.

"It is a recruitment video. Whether he frames it that way for himself or not," she tells The Feed.

Lowe says some neurodivergent people have vulnerabilities that recruiters learn to recognise.

"For a lot of neurodivergent people, one of the things they really struggle with is social interactions and kind of understanding what people mean and the various layers of communication," she says.

"One thing that extremist groups do is they accept you. 'If you want to come, we're going to accept you. And not only are we going to accept you, you become part of a brotherhood.'"

Sewell dismisses expert understanding of autism repeatedly in his videos — "none of these experts understand autism" — and argues instead that those...
body.zh: 在我们的 YouTube 频道上观看完整的纪录片“自闭症、极端主义和招募”。 “阿道夫·希特勒，巨大的自闭症患者，巨大的自闭症患者，就像所有这些令人难以置信的人一样，是有史以来最优秀的人，”托马斯·休厄尔在网上告诉观众。 休厄尔是一位新纳粹分子，领导着国家社会主义网络 (NSN)（现为白澳大利亚），他在长达 22 分钟的独白中讲述了他对自闭症的“看法”。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 “我们过去欺负书呆子，现在却溺爱他们。现在我们会说，‘哦，你有残疾。你是自闭症患者。’”我们对待他们就好像他们是弱智一样。” 休厄尔反复重申，自闭症男性不需要受到区别对待，而是需要挑战、男性榜样并“引导他们的固着”。他建议参军——休厄尔本人也曾退伍——学习一门手艺或接受高等教育。 贯穿他的评论的是休厄尔自己的运动。他向观众讲述了一名前 NSN 成员的故事，他说他曾将他置于自己的保护之下。 “我变得像他的哥哥一样，我教他如何举重，我教他如何打架，我教他如何与女孩交谈，经过两年的激烈欺凌……他变得像一个正常人一样。” 一年后，即 2025 年，休厄尔分享了另一个谈论自闭症的视频。这次他批评的是一项反暴力极端主义计划。 “我招募了数百名自闭症青少年，其中零人刺伤过任何人，”休厄尔开玩笑说。 我们联系了休厄尔，他否认自己曾积极招募自闭症患者。 但在他发表上述言论之际，澳大利亚联邦警察（法新社）和研究人员强调，极端主义团体以年轻人为目标，他们认为年轻人是弱势群体，包括那些神经分歧的人。 佩塔·洛（Peta Lowe）多年来一直领导新南威尔士州政府针对年轻人的打击暴力极端主义计划，他对这段视频毫不怀疑。 “这是一段招聘视频。无论他是否是为了自己而这样设计的，”她告诉 The Feed。 洛说，一些神经分歧的人有一些弱点，招聘人员要学会识别这些弱点。 “对于许多神经分歧的人来说，他们真正面临的困难之一是社交互动以及理解人们的意思和各个层面的沟通，”她说。 “极端主义团体所做的一件事就是他们接受你。‘如果你想来，我们就会接受你。我们不仅会接受你，你还会成为兄弟会的一部分。’” 休厄尔在他的视频中反复驳斥了专家对自闭症的理解——“这些专家都不理解自闭症”——并认为那些……

The principle of speaking for those who cannot speak for themselves, as found in Proverbs 31:8, calls us to protect the vulnerable from manipulation and harm. Yahweh calls us to ensure that the voices of the vulnerable are never...

title.en: NSW’s koala national park will protect threatened species and cap logging across the state. Could the Greens really block it? | Adam Morton
title.zh: 新南威尔士州的考拉国家公园将保护受威胁物种并限制全州伐木。绿党真的会阻止它吗？

summary.en: The Albanese government approved a proposal allowing the park to create carbon credits worth hundreds of millions of dollars, sparking a schism among environmentalists.
summary.zh: 阿尔巴尼斯政府批准了一项提案，允许该公园创造价值数亿美元的碳信用，这在环保主义者中引发了分歧。

body.en:
Is it when a huge forest area that is home to a stack of threatened species, including koalas, and has been the focus of years and years of campaigning, is protected from logging?

Or does it depend on how the battle is won – for example, if it lets companies claim that the forest is helping cut their pollution?

It sounds like the start of a philosophical debate, but isn’t. It’s at the heart of a dispute dividing environment and climate activists, and is being weighed by the Greens ahead of a vote in the Senate next month.

In blunt terms, the minor party is considering whether to make an extraordinary call: to support a Nationals motion to strike down a Labor plan that would create a long-discussed great koala national park in northern New South Wales, and significantly reduce native forest logging in the state.

The vote was scheduled for last week but – in a sign of how vexed the issue has become – has been delayed until next month after the Greens asked the Nationals for more time to reach a consensus position.

In terms of a national political debate, the issue hasn’t had much of a look-in yet. But the ramifications could be substantial.

The story starts with a grassroots campaign to create a large park around Coffs Harbour to protect forests and more than a hundred threatened species, including koalas, gliders and glossy black cockatoos. That campaign is backed by a range of local campaigners and First Nations leaders.

NSW Labor signed up as a supporter more than a decade ago while in opposition. Under the premier, Chris Minns , it wasn’t until September 2025 that it announced it would add 176,000 hectares of state forest – an area more than twice the size of Canberra – to existing protected areas to create a 476,000 hectare reserve. It is said to protect about 12,000 koalas, water catchments and carbon stores.

The final confirmation that the park would go ahead didn’t come until June , when the Albanese government approved a NSW proposal that allows it to use the park to create carbon credits worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

Carbon credits remain opaque to most people, but they are the centre of the Australian government’s climate change policy. We need to explain why (bear with me here).

Each credit is said to represent one tonne of greenhouse gas emissions that has been prevented or drawn down from the atmosphere. In Australia, they most often come from projects that are meant to regenerate forests in the outback and capture and burn methane released from landfill sites.

The goal of the projects is sound. Regenerating forests is good! Cutting methane pollution is good! But the projects themselves have been sharply criticised.

Scientific studies have found major shortcomings with the main types of projects used in Australia and...
body.zh: 是不是当一片巨大的森林地区受到保护，免遭砍伐时，这里栖息着包括考拉在内的许多受威胁物种，并且多年来一直是运动的焦点？ 还是取决于这场战斗如何获胜——例如，是否可以让公司声称森林正在帮助减少污染？ 这听起来像是一场哲学辩论的开始，但事实并非如此。这是环境和气候活动人士之间争论的核心，绿党在下个月参议院投票之前正在权衡这一问题。 坦白说，这个小党正在考虑是否发出特别呼吁：支持国家党一项动议，否决一项工党计划，该计划将在新南威尔士州北部建立一个讨论已久的大考拉国家公园，并大幅减少该州的原生森林采伐。 投票原定于上周举行，但在绿党要求国民队有更多时间达成共识后，投票被推迟到下个月，这表明这个问题已经变得多么棘手。 就全国政治辩论而言，这个问题还没有得到太多关注。但其影响可能是巨大的。 故事始于一场草根运动，旨在在科夫斯港周围创建一个大型公园，以保护森林和一百多种受威胁的物种，包括考拉、滑翔机和光泽的黑色凤头鹦鹉。该活动得到了一系列当地活动人士和原住民领导人的支持。 新南威尔士州工党十多年前在反对党时期就加入了支持者行列。在州长克里斯·明斯 (Chris Minns) 的领导下，直到 2025 年 9 月，澳大利亚才宣布将在现有保护区的基础上增加 176,000 公顷的国家森林（面积是堪培拉面积的两倍多），以创建 476,000 公顷的保护区。据说它可以保护大约 12,000 只考拉、集水区和碳储存。 直到六月，阿尔巴尼亚政府才最终确认该公园将继续建设，当时阿尔巴尼亚政府批准了新南威尔士州的一项提案，允许其利用该公园创造价值数亿澳元的碳信用额。 碳信用额对大多数人来说仍然不透明，但它们是澳大利亚政府气候变化政策的核心。我们需要解释一下原因（请耐心听我说）。 据说每个信用额代表已被阻止或从大气中减少的一吨温室气体排放量。在澳大利亚，它们通常来自旨在再生内陆森林并捕获和燃烧垃圾填埋场释放的甲烷的项目。 这些项目的目标是合理的。恢复森林是好事！减少甲烷污染是好事！但这些项目本身却遭到了严厉批评。 科学研究发现澳大利亚使用的主要项目类型存在重大缺陷......

reflection.en: The proposed koala national park in NSW highlights a complex ethical debate among environmentalists: whether protecting threatened species through carbon credits is truly beneficial if it allows companies to offset their pollution. This tension between a good outcome and potentially problematic means resonates with the biblical principle that while many...
reflection.zh: 新南威尔士州拟议的考拉国家公园引发了环保主义者之间复杂的伦理辩论：通过碳信用保护受威胁物种，如果这允许公司抵消其污染，是否真正有益。这种良好结果与潜在问题手段之间的张力，与圣经原则“凡事都可行，但不都有益处；凡事都可行，但不都造就人”相呼应。当绿党权衡他们的投票时，挑战在于不仅要辨别什么是可行的，还要辨别什么能真正造就受造物并促进真正的管家职分。

summary.en: Residents in West Footscray, Melbourne, are reporting significant disruptions from a newly constructed NextDC data center located 300 meters from residential homes. The facility brings constant humming noise and light pollution, leading to calls for better planning protections for existing communities.
summary.zh: 墨尔本西富茨克雷的居民反映，距离住宅区仅300米的新建 NextDC 数据中心造成了严重干扰。该设施带来了持续的嗡嗡声和光污染，引发了人们呼吁为现有社区提供更好的规划保护。

body.en:
When Sean Brown moved to West Footscray two years ago, days after his son was born, he thought he'd found a good spot to raise a family — green space, a train station nearby, and a community with room to grow.

Instead, his home is now 300 metres from one of the largest data centres in the country.

"It's a massive black box in the middle of a residential area. There's this visual heaviness to it that you can't really escape," Brown tells SBS News.

NextDC's M3 facility in the Melbourne suburb brings a constant humming noise audible even 100m away, he says, while ongoing construction means near-constant light, noise and disruption.

Parking is scarce with facility workers competing for street spots, and Brown says whole streets have lost power for full days at a time during infrastructure works, with little warning and no compensation. He's also worried about health risks, and the future of his entire suburb.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Branded by its chief executive, Craig Scroggie, as "Australia's largest hyperscale AI factory", the M3 site is set to double in size by 2027 — covering 10 hectares in size, and drawing 225MW of power, 24 hours a day.

A separate facility, the Perri Melbourne Data Centre (PMDC), has been approved and planned just a few blocks over.

There are currently 162 operational data centres across Australia, with a further 90 proposed, according to the Climate Council — and it's unclear whether planned rules to data centres in residential areas will apply to any of them.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will use a speech to the Business Council of Australia's annual dinner on Tuesday night to announce new national rules that would block future data centres from being built near homes, schools, or prime agricultural land.

Developers will also be required to add more renewable energy to the grid than their data centres consume, minimise water use, and ensure new sites are appropriate for their size — avoiding land that could otherwise be used for housing.

"Australia is in a strong position to attract investment in data centres, but maintaining social licence will be essential," Albanese will say.

"That means ensuring energy bills do not rise, water security is maintained and locations are appropriate."

Asked about communities already living with data centres, Albanese did not directly answer when pressed on ABC Perth on Tuesday, instead pointing to the same social licence framework.

Asked by SBS News whether any measures would target existing sites or address community concern that the new rules don't cover people already affected, the prime minister's office declined to comment.

This situation illustrates that while a project may be legally 'lawful,' it is not necessarily 'beneficial' if it fails to build up the surrounding community. We are called to consider how our advancements...
reflection.zh: 肖恩·布朗原本希望在宁静的社区抚养儿子，但这一愿望被巨大数据中心的“视觉沉重感”和持续噪音打破了。这种情况说明，虽然一个项目在法律上可能是“可行的”，但如果它不能造就周围的社区，就不一定是“有益的”。我们受召去思考我们的进步如何影响邻舍平静的生活，确保技术的发展不会以牺牲人类的福祉为代价。

verse.textEn: "I have the right to do anything," you say — but not everything is beneficial. "I have the right to do anything" — but not everything is constructive.

title.en: The 'extraordinarily expensive' project reshaping a state — and drawing political battlelines
title.zh: “极其昂贵”的项目正在重塑一个州——并划定政治战线

summary.en: Victoria's Premier Ben Carroll has announced a $2 billion reduction in the cost of the state's largest infrastructure project, the Suburban Rail Loop. This pivot comes amid ongoing debate over the project's "extraordinarily expensive" nature, its disputed economic benefits, and its lengthy construction timeline.
summary.zh: 维多利亚州州长本·卡罗尔宣布，将该州最大的基础设施项目——城郊铁路环线（SRL）的成本削减20亿澳元。这一调整是在该项目“极其昂贵”、经济效益存在争议以及建设周期漫长等问题持续引发辩论之际做出的。

body.en:
Victorian Premier Ben Carroll has announced $2 billion in cuts to the state's largest infrastructure project, the Suburban Rail Loop (SRL), saying: "I respect your money."

His comments underline the controversy over the 90km underground rapid transit project, which will link Melbourne's middle suburbs and allow passengers to travel across the city without passing through the CBD.

The state government says the mega-project will reshape Melbourne into a multi-nodal city, bringing services and jobs closer to where people live, building more homes, and creating more jobs.

But its enormous cost, disputed economic benefits and lengthy construction timeline have also made it one of Australia's most controversial infrastructure projects.

Liam Davies, a lecturer in sustainability and urban planning at RMIT University, said the SRL was a step towards transforming Melbourne's city-centric public transport system into an interconnected network.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Melbourne's greatest challenge is that it has become an extraordinarily large city, physically," he told SBS News.

"We can't just adopt the transport strategy for a denser, more compact city like London. We need to do something of our own, and the SRL is an attempt to do that in a Melburnian context."

With Labor and the Coalition deeply divided on the SRL, the project's future could be decided when Victorians head to the polls in November.

The SRL will connect Melbourne's middle suburbs from Cheltenham in the south-east to Werribee in the west via Melbourne Airport through a 90km underground rail line.

The project is split into three stages. The first section — SRL East — is under construction, running from Cheltenham to Box Hill via six new underground stations. The first trains are expected by 2035.

Critics argue the mega-project's business case doesn't stack up, and the multi-billion-dollar price tag is a financial liability for Victoria, which has the second-highest debt per capita of any state or territory, behind the Northern Territory.

More than $33 billion has already been invested in SRL East, according to the premier.

A Parliamentary Budget Office analysis puts the price tag for building the East and North sections at $96.4 billion, though there is currently no fully costed estimate for the entire project, which includes the final stage, SRL West.

An evaluation last year by Infrastructure Australia — an advisory body to the federal government — found the SRL's business case was insufficiently detailed and relied on future stages to justify its benefits.

reflection.en: The Victorian government's decision to cut $2 billion from the Suburban Rail Loop, with Premier Ben Carroll stating "I respect your money," underscores the immense challenge of wise stewardship in large public projects. When leaders face "extraordinarily expensive" and contentious decisions that draw "political battlelines," the need for clear judgment is...

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: 'Get it out': ARIA to ban AI-generated music from Australian charts
title.zh: 澳大利亚唱片业协会禁止人工智能生成的音乐进入排行榜

summary.en: ARIA has updated its code of practice to ensure that only songs that are "substantially human-made" qualify for the Australian music charts. Chief executive Annabelle Herd stated that the charts exist to celebrate human artistry and success, rather than unlicensed AI output.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚唱片业协会（ARIA）更新了其行业准则，规定只有“基本上由人类创作”的歌曲才有资格进入澳大利亚音乐排行榜。首席执行官安娜贝尔·赫德表示，排行榜旨在庆祝人类的艺术造诣和成就，而非未经授权的人工智能产出。

body.en:
Music will need to be "substantially human-made" in order to qualify for Australia's main music chart, in an industry bid to stamp out AI-generated tracks.

Songs wholly generated using artificial intelligence will no longer be eligible for the ARIA charts from Friday, in an update to The Australian Recording Industry Association's (ARIA) code of practice.

ARIA chief executive Annabelle Herd said a chart that rewards unlicensed AI output would "undercut the very basis of the recorded music we exist to present".

"The ARIA charts are about tracking consumption and sales of music in Australia, but they're also about celebrating human artistry and success," Herd told ABC radio.

"We're not particularly interested in including AI-generated music as part of that process, particularly when it's taking up a spot from an Australian artist in the chart."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

AI-assisted songs will still feature on the charts, but they must be substantially human-made and raise no stream or chart manipulation concerns.

"I'm sure that there are a lot of artists that are using AI tools to enhance creativity, to do really cool, new, exciting things," Herd said.

"Artists have always been at the forefront of new tech ... it's made some of the best music ever created, and no doubt AI will create some really exciting evolution of that."

Songs on the ARIA charts that use AI include Gold Coast-based DJ and producer Josh Fawaz's dance track Like a Prayer, which is fourth on the ARIA's top 20 Australian singles after peaking at number two in May.

A dance cover of Madonna's 1989 hit, generative AI is credited for the drums and vocals on the track, according to Spotify.

Australian electronic band Peking Duk supported the association's call to outlaw generative AI from the charts, claiming it was "removing the human experience from life".

"AI is using our stuff. It's using a lot of our peers' stuff, you know, people we know," band member Adam Hyde told Channel Nine's Today show .

"There is so much good art in Australia and something like AI coming along and kind of sweeping the charts and all that jazz, it's like, get it out."

ARIA's decision heeds global AI principles drawn up by the record industry's peak body, The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry, in July.

The federation said the guidelines would be rolled out to official charts in Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia and advocated to more than 20 other official chart programs in Europe and the Pacific, including the ARIAs.

body.zh: 音乐需要“实质上是人造的”才能有资格进入澳大利亚主要音乐排行榜，行业努力消除人工智能生成的曲目。 根据澳大利亚唱片工业协会 (ARIA) 行为准则的更新，从周五开始，完全使用人工智能生成的歌曲将不再符合 ARIA 排行榜的资格。 ARIA 首席执行官安娜贝尔·赫德 (Annabelle Herd) 表示，奖励未经许可的人工智能输出的图表将“削弱我们现有的录制音乐的基础”。 “ARIA 排行榜旨在追踪澳大利亚音乐的消费和销售，但它们也旨在庆祝人类的艺术和成功，”赫德告诉美国广播公司广播电台。 “我们对将人工智能生成的音乐纳入这一过程并不是特别感兴趣，特别是当它在排行榜上占据了澳大利亚艺术家的位置时。” 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 人工智能辅助的歌曲仍将出现在排行榜上，但它们必须基本上是人造的，并且不会引起流媒体或排行榜操纵问题。 “我确信有很多艺术家正在使用人工智能工具来增强创造力，做一些非常酷、新、令人兴奋的事情，”赫德说。 “艺术家一直走在新技术的最前沿……它创造了一些有史以来最好的音乐，毫无疑问，人工智能将创造一些真正令人兴奋的演变。” ARIA 排行榜上使用人工智能的歌曲包括黄金海岸 DJ 兼制作人 Josh Fawaz 的舞曲《Like a Prayer》，该歌曲在 5 月份达到峰值第二名后，在 ARIA 前 20 名澳大利亚单曲中排名第四。 据 Spotify 称，麦当娜 1989 年的热门歌曲的舞曲翻唱，歌曲中的鼓和人声均归功于生成人工智能。 澳大利亚电子乐队 Peking Duk 支持该协会从排行榜上取缔生成式人工智能的呼吁，声称它“消除了人类的生活体验”。 “人工智能正在使用我们的东西。它正在使用我们很多同行的东西，你知道，我们认识的人，”乐队成员亚当·海德告诉第九频道的今日节目。 “澳大利亚有很多优秀的艺术，像人工智能这样的东西正在出现，席卷了排行榜，所有的爵士乐，就像，把它拿出来。” ARIA 的决定考虑了唱片行业最高机构国际唱片业联合会于 7 月制定的全球人工智能原则。 该联合会表示，该指南将推广到拉丁美洲、中东、非洲和东南亚的官方排行榜，并推广到欧洲和太平洋地区的 20 多个其他官方排行榜项目，包括 ARIA。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: By insisting that music remain "substantially human-made," ARIA reminds us that art is more than just a pleasing arrangement of sounds; it is an expression of the human soul. Scripture teaches that we are created in the image of Yahweh, the ultimate Creator, which gives our creative work a dignity that machines cannot replicate. Protecting the space for...
reflection.zh: 澳大利亚唱片业协会坚持音乐必须“基本上由人类创作”，这提醒我们，艺术不仅仅是悦耳声音的排列，更是人类灵魂的表达。圣经教导我们，我们是按照创造主雅伟的形象造的，这赋予了人类创作一种机器无法复制的尊严。保护人类艺术创作的空间，正是对上帝安置在我们里面的独特生命火花和创作意图的尊重。

title.en: How mainland Chinese engineers can help Hong Kong firms bridge talent gap
title.zh: 内地工程师如何助力香港企业弥补人才缺口

summary.en: Industry leaders highlighted how mainland China's extensive pool of engineers can assist Hong Kong companies in expanding and scaling operations. During a six-day tour of the Greater Bay Area, officials and researchers visited key facilities in Guangzhou and Dongguan to discuss bridging the talent gap.
summary.zh: 行业领袖表示，中国内地庞大的工程师人才库可以帮助香港公司扩张、弥补人才缺口并扩大运营规模。在由港澳办组织的为期六天的粤港澳大湾区媒体访问活动中，与会者分享了相关见解。行程包括参观广州南沙的研究机构以及东莞的货运设施和大学。

title.en: Store slapped with 30-day ban over forced shopping
title.zh: 商店因强迫购物被禁30天

summary.en: A company linked to forced shopping has been banned from receiving inbound tour groups for 30 days. The Travel Industry Authority said on Tuesday that the suspension of Kaiser Jewellery International Limited, which is registered under the Administrative Scheme for Registered...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自香港栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: A company linked to forced shopping has been banned from receiving inbound tour groups for 30 days. The Travel Industry Authority said on Tuesday that the suspension of Kaiser Jewellery International Limited, which is registered under the Administrative Scheme for Registered Shops for Inbound Tour Groups, will last from Wednesday to September 24. The shop sells various items including jewellery and clothing. The authority said it had failed to prevent forced shopping involving mainland visitors in February. It also failed to take appropriate measures to ensure that no unauthorised personnel would carry out promotional activities inside the store, the authority added. The watchdog said it has zero tolerance for forced shopping and any behaviour that damages the reputation of Hong Kong’s tourism industry. It also ordered directors, managers and all frontline staff of the shop to complete training courses within a month. The authority added that it had engaged in exchanges with mainland authorities to step up supervision. DAB lawmaker Nixie Lam welcomed the 30-day suspension, saying any misconduct that harms tourists’ interests and damages Hong Kong’s image must be punished. “It does send a pretty powerful industry-wide reminder that those registered shops cannot simply just profit from doing this sort of thing,” she told RTHK. “I think it is important for all those shop owners and also their shop staff to understand that pressuring visitors or having all these sort of illegal acts are something that we really need to stop immediately.” She added that all registered shops authorised to receive tour groups are duty-bound to protect the interests of travellers. Edited by Edmond Fong
body.zh: 一家涉嫌强迫购物的公司被禁止接待入境旅游团30天。旅游业监管局周二表示，根据入境旅游团注册店铺管理计划注册的凯撒珠宝国际有限公司将暂停营业，为期周三至9月24日。该店出售珠宝和服装等多种商品。当局表示，二月份未能阻止大陆游客被迫购物。当局补充说，该公司也未能采取适当措施确保未经授权的人员不会在店内进行促销活动。该监管机构表示，对强制购物以及任何损害香港旅游业声誉的行为采取零容忍态度。并要求该店的董事、经理和所有一线员工在一个月内完成培训课程。该局补充说，已与内地当局进行交流，以加强监管。民建联议员林郑月娥对暂停30天表示欢迎，并表示任何损害游客利益和损害香港形象的不当行为都必须受到惩罚。 “这确实向全行业发出了一个非常有力的提醒，即那些注册商店不能仅仅通过做这种事情来获利，”她告诉香港电台。 “我认为，对于所有店主和店员来说，了解向游客施压或所有这些非法行为是我们真正需要立即停止的事情，这一点很重要。”她补充说，所有有权接待旅行团的注册商店都有责任保护游客的利益。埃德蒙·方编辑

title.en: Crunch culture and tight timelines blamed for 15 construction site deaths this year
title.zh: 今年香港建筑工地因“紧迫文化”和严格工期导致15人死亡

summary.en: Construction industry representatives in Hong Kong have attributed 15 fatal worksite accidents this year to a pervasive "crunch culture" and tight timelines. Union chair Chau Sze-kit explained that this environment pushes management to prioritize speed and convenience, leading to shortcuts on safety procedures to meet...
summary.zh: 香港建筑业代表将今年发生的15起致命工地事故归咎于普遍存在的“紧迫文化”和严格的工期。工会主席周思杰解释说，这种环境促使管理层优先考虑速度和便利，为了赶工期和避免罚款，从而在安全程序上走捷径。

body.en: Construction sector representatives have blamed the industry’s crunch culture for the 15 fatal worksite accidents recorded in Hong Kong since the beginning of this year. Construction workers in Hong Kong. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Speaking on RTHK radio, Hong Kong Construction Industry Employees General Union chair Chau Sze-kit said that aloof attitudes toward occupational safety stem from a pervasive culture of rushing work at construction sites, pushing workers to prioritise convenience and foregoing precautions. “When frontline management faces deadlines and potential penalties, they may choose to take shortcuts on certain safety procedures,” Chau said in Cantonese. Chau also said the industry-wide practice of awarding contracts to the lowest bidder meant safety was sacrificed for speed, adding that contractors may offload the pressure they face to subcontractors who have “no bargaining power.” Speaking on the same RTHK programme, Lawrence Ng, chair of the Construction Workers Registration Board at the Construction Industry Council, said that worksite bosses are often pressed to get more done in less time to compensate for increasingly frequent delays caused by extreme weather. A worker at a construction site in Hong Kong on February 13, 2023. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. He cited a survey conducted by the Council indicating that 5 to 7 per cent of frontline managers and workers have “extremely weak” safety awareness. Safety culture Ng’s remarks come a day after Construction Industry Council chairperson Thomas Ho said during a construction safety event that worksite fatalities are continuing to climb in spite of harsher penalties levied against negligent employers. In April 2023, Hong Kong amended the Occupational Safety and Occupational Health Legislation Ordinance , raising the maximum penalty for employers who commit serious safety violations from HK$500,000 to HK$10 million. Violators also face up to two years in prison. Ho said the 15 deaths so far this year was an increase compared to before the penalty was raised. “Safety culture hasn’t made its way to the worksite,” Ho said in Cantonese. “Out of the 15 [fatalities]… even a safety supervisor died. Why? Because we have only paid lip service and haven’t truly fulfilled our responsibility.” Construction workers in Hong Kong. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Crunch culture is one of the biggest killers on construction sites,” he added. Delivering an address at the same event, Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said that worksite accidents more broadly had decreased by 20 per cent between 2023 and 2025, following the implementation of the “4S” Smart Site Safety System. This enables early identification of potential safety hazards through smart devices and communication networks for...

The practice of finning live sharks and discarding their bodies is banned in much of the Pacific but continues due to demand in Asia. The vessel was...
summary.zh: 据基里巴斯海事警察称，与北京关系日益密切的太平洋小国基里巴斯本月扣押了一艘中国渔船，因其非法捕捞鱼翅。将活鲨鱼割鳍并将其尸体丢弃的做法在太平洋大部分地区被禁止，但由于亚洲的需求而持续存在。该船是8月3日至14日期间由11个太平洋岛国进行的一次监视行动中扣押的四艘船只之一，美国海岸警卫队和一架澳大利亚军用飞机在部分地区提...

body.en: Kiribati, a tiny Pacific neighbour to Hawaii that has grown ties with Beijing, detained a Chinese vessel this month for illegally harvesting shark fins, its maritime police told AFP. Sharks. File photo: Klaus Stiefel/Flickr. The practice of cutting fins off live sharks and throwing the carcasses back into the sea is banned in much of the Pacific Ocean, but persists due to demand in East and Southeast Asia. The Chinese ship was among four vessels detained in a surveillance crackdown by 11 Pacific island nations between August 3 to 14, assisted by the US Coast Guard in some areas and an Australian military aircraft. Kiribati, however, operates its own patrol boat. The vessel was licensed to ply Kiribati’s waters but was detained by the maritime police after inspectors found shark fins on board, commander Tom Redfern told AFP. “It was escorted back to Christmas Island for further investigation,” he said, referring to a large atoll belonging to Kiribati and located south of Hawaii. Kiribati has an exclusive economic zone spanning 3.5 million square kilometres (1.4 million square miles) of ocean, and has drawn interest from Chinese state companies since switching diplomatic ties from Taiwan in 2019. A Kiribati flag. Photo: Kahunapule Michael Johnson/Flickr. It also hosts Chinese police, a decision the United States has said risks fuelling regional tensions. “A Kiribati Police maritime boarding officer, not under a shiprider agreement, boarded and inspected it, finding that the vessel was breaching its condition of licence by keeping and retaining shark fins onboard,” said Redfern. Kiribati has recently strengthened cooperation with France, with French military personnel due to arrive next month on Christmas Island to rebuild local police stations. The practice of removing shark fins is banned across the region. Andrew Chin, a fisheries researcher at Australia’s James Cook University, said finning had led to “massive declines” in shark numbers, prompting stringent controls in the Pacific. A bowl of shark fin soup. Photo: Janine Cheung/Flickr. “Because it is now illegal, if people are doing it, it is going to be hidden and really hard to detect,” he said. Research on the DNA of thousands of shark fins sold in Hong Kong markets pointed to its origins in the region. “We have seen evidence of illegal trade from the western and eastern sides of the Pacific,” Demian Chapman, who conducted the research as director of the Sharks and Rays Conservation Research Program at Mote Marine Laboratory in Florida, said. There have been other cases of Chinese vessels violating the finning ban, he told AFP. Reduced demand in China for shark fin soup, including a ban on serving it at government functions,...

body.en: Two activists who organised commemorations of the bloody crackdown on China’s 1989 pro-democracy protests now face jail. Remembering is not a crime For decades, Hong Kong mourned when the mainland could not. Its huge annual Tiananmen vigil kept alive the memory of the 1989 pro-reform protests in Beijing, and of the massacre that suppressed them. summary.en: As part of its efforts to map out Europe's science-policy interface for biodiversity, a paper on the correlation between governance objectives for safeguarding the biosphere and on-the-ground realities for select species groups has been published. The work is in the journal...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

As part of its efforts to map out Europe's science-policy interface for biodiversity, a paper on the correlation between governance objectives for safeguarding the biosphere and on-the-ground realities for select species groups has been published . The work is in the journal Nature Ecology & Evolution .

Among the group of 36 authors (affiliated with 38 research entities) are seven consortium members of the project. At the National Research Institute on Agriculture, Food & the Environment (INRAE), this includes the study's lead, postdoctoral fellow Stanislas Rigal, as well as Sandra Luque, Maxime Lenormand and Léa Tardieu. Other BioAgora contributors include Tristan Bakx and Lluis Brotons from CREAF and Josef Settele from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ).

The study analyzes the effects of climate, land use and land-use intensity on 263 common bird species and 144 common butterfly species using observations from more than 20,000 sites across 26 European countries from 2000 to 2021. These species are modeled to understand how their development would be shaped by alternative land-use futures based on the IPBES Nature Futures Framework—Nature for Nature (NFN), Nature for Society (NFS) and Nature as Culture (NAC)—combined with the most sustainability-oriented climate and socioeconomic pathway, SSP1 ("Green Road"), from the IPCC. These scenarios thus allow projections of potential changes in common biodiversity across Europe through 2050.

The paper shows that none of the conservation scenarios assessed is sufficient to halt, let alone reverse, the projected decline in the average abundance of common bird and butterfly species. This remains true even under the most biodiversity-friendly scenarios incorporating key EU policies, including the EU's 2030 Biodiversity Strategy, 2030 Forest Strategy and Farm to Fork Strategy.

The decline is particularly pronounced for farmland birds, while grassland butterflies continue to face strong pressures from agricultural intensification and land abandonment. Climate change exacerbates these circumstances, with particularly negative effects on butterflies. Forest species fare relatively better, partly because of expanding forest cover, although intensive forest management continues to increase even under conservation-oriented scenarios.

Importantly, the benefits of conservation scenarios are unevenly distributed across Europe, with stronger improvements projected in Western and Northern Europe and more limited positive effects in eastern and southern regions, where agricultural pressures are increasing.

summary.en: Researchers are gauging the effectiveness of electron beams in the fight against foodborne pathogens in poultry. "Impact of Electron Beam (eBeam) Treatment on Meat Quality and Sensory Attributes of Ground Chicken and Turkey" is published in the journal Poultry Science. At the...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

Researchers are gauging the effectiveness of electron beams in the fight against foodborne pathogens in poultry. "Impact of Electron Beam (eBeam) Treatment on Meat Quality and Sensory Attributes of Ground Chicken and Turkey" is published in the journal Poultry Science . At the heart of the study is eBeam , a nonthermal technology that uses high-energy electron beams to cause irreparable damage to pathogen DNA.

Foodborne illness is no small thing. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said it typically coordinates 17–36 investigations of foodborne illnesses each week. In a study, the CDC said that seven foodborne pathogens accounted for 53,300 hospitalizations and 931 deaths in 2019 alone.

Along with X-rays and gamma rays, eBeam is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for "cold pasteurization"—a germ-killing technique that doesn't rely on heat.

X-rays, gamma rays and electron beams have been used for decades "for pathogen control in fresh, frozen and refrigerated food," said Palmy Jesudhasan, a research microbiologist at the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Agricultural Research Service.

Currently, irradiated fruits and spices are on grocery shelves, and Omaha Steaks and Schwan's use irradiation to pasteurize beef, Jesudhasan said. However, the technology's use in "poultry still lacks the data to build confidence" in its use.

"We started with ground poultry because it is a major source of salmonella and campylobacter and a key driver of recalls," Jesudhasan said.

The study had dual goals: First, to understand the ability of eBeam technology to reduce or control food pathogens and, second, to evaluate the effects of irradiation treatment on meat quality, he said.

The research team used the world's largest electron beam irradiator at the National Center for Electron Beam Research, housed at Texas A&M University.

"eBeam is mainly used for sterilization purposes," Jesudhasan said. "When you expose any cells, whether it's human cells, bacterial cells or virus to the beam, it hits the nucleus and shreds DNA or RNA so bacteria cannot replicate."

Jesudhasan said the process "could also generate other reactive oxygen species that can also cause not-so-good side effects for the bacteria."

"We don't want to use too much of a dose," he said. "When you use too much, it might make the product bad."

While the electron beam doesn't heat or cook the meat, its oxidizing qualities bear watching, especially in poultry, said Casey Owens, professor and meat scientist for the University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture.

title.en: Relentless heat and drought take a toll on herders' physical and mental health, in Kenya and the US
title.zh: 持续高温与干旱严重损害肯尼亚和美国牧民的身心健康

summary.en: Researchers report that herders in northern Kenya and the United States are facing unprecedented heat and drought, which severely impacts their physical ability to work and their mental well-being. The study highlights the struggle of those who must remain outdoors with their livestock despite rising temperatures.
summary.zh: 研究人员报告称，肯尼亚北部和美国的牧民正面临前所未有的高温和干旱，这严重影响了他们的体力劳动能力和心理健康。该研究强调了那些尽管气温升高仍必须带着牲畜留在户外的人们所面临的困境。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

If being outside in the heat for even a few minutes felt miserable this summer, imagine what it's like for herders who are always out walking with their livestock and rarely get a break.

"We have never experienced such hot days," a woman herder in northern Kenya told our research team in 2024. "It is difficult to [do things] outside [with] the high temperatures."

Her experience is echoed by herders in both the U.S. and Kenya, where we study health and climate. Our team's recent data from Kenya suggest that when drought and heat are particularly bad, herders suffer heat-related illness and symptoms of anxiety and depression.

While fewer data are available about herders in the U.S., there is reason to worry about them as global temperatures rise .

In northern Kenya, herders spend much of their lives outdoors with their animals. During dry seasons, herders can move 100 miles (roughly 160 kilometers) with their livestock , sleeping under the stars or in makeshift shacks along the way.

In the U.S., shepherds on the open range often live similar lives . Most hold temporary visas and are paid by their employers to spend 24 hours a day, seven days a week with flocks of sheep. They often live in portable trailers with no air conditioning, and they spend long hours in the direct sun in states like Colorado and California .

Herding is a livelihood designed for high temperatures —the animals can be moved to where there's food and water as needed.

However, drought and extremely hot summers can mean less food and water for livestock—and more extreme temperatures. As herders search for water and pasture, they may walk with the animals for almost 12 hours a day in the sun, one Kenyan herder told our team.

In Kenya, pastoralists have a higher risk of dehydration at high ambient temperatures, which have become more frequent . In California, extreme temperatures have become more common too . A state report warned that herders can die from heat-related illness and underscored that employers must have heat illness prevention plans with precautions like prompt emergency responses .

Because they are so isolated, herders may only go to the doctor when badly injured or very sick , so researchers usually only get brief glimpses into herders' health and how it's affected by heat exposure. In the U.S., often only herders' employers know where they are and may visit them only once every couple of weeks .

When the pastures dry up and the heat becomes relentless, it tests both the body's endurance and the spirit's hope. In such seasons of scarcity, we are called to look to Yahweh for a strength...

title.en: Trust launches 'first-of-its-kind' nature survey
title.zh: 信托基金发起“史无前例”的自然调查

summary.en: A wildlife group says "everyone can get involved with protecting nature" by taking part in research.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A wildlife trust has said it has launched a first-of-its-kind survey to help find out how people feel about nature and guide future conservation efforts.

The Suffolk Wildlife Trust (SWT), in collaboration with the University of Suffolk, has brought out the Great Suffolk Nature Survey, which quizzes participants on the county's "struggling" wildlife.

It asks about their experiences with local wildlife, how they get involved with local nature, and their attitudes towards conservation, climate change and environmental projects.

The short survey comes weeks after a devastating wildfire at Dunwich Heath and nearby RSPB Minsmere destroyed vital wildlife habitats, which could take years to recover.

Jack Cripps, head of marketing and communications at SWT, said: "The county's landscapes and wildlife are a huge part of what I and so many others who live here are proud of.

"But our wildlife is struggling and we're really starting to feel the impacts of our changing climate. This survey will go a bit deeper into what local people think and feel about nature.

"Everyone can get involved with protecting nature, and the results of the survey will guide Suffolk Wildlife Trust's future community projects and campaigning."

This is the first time SWT has run its own survey, although it has previously gathered local responses as part of the nationwide The Great Big Nature Survey.

Hannah Page, from the University of Suffolk, said it was "delighted" to be supporting the trust with the "important project".

She also said there would be an opportunity for a student from the university to help roll out the survey thanks to a paid student placement from the county council.

title.en: Shingles vaccine linked to 24% lower dementia risk
title.zh: 带状疱疹疫苗与痴呆症风险降低24%相关

summary.en: Older adults who received the Shingrix shingles vaccine were 24% less likely to be diagnosed with dementia over four years in a study of more than 500,000 people. Researchers estimate the difference could amount to roughly one dementia case prevented for every 17 people, suggesting a significant secondary benefit to...
summary.zh: 一项针对超过50万人的研究显示，接种Shingrix带状疱疹疫苗的老年人在四年内被诊断出患有痴呆症的可能性降低了24%。研究人员估计，每17名接种疫苗的人中就可能减少一例痴呆症病例，这表明该疫苗具有显著的额外健康益处。

body.en:
Older adults who received a shingles vaccine after entering a skilled nursing facility were less likely to be diagnosed with dementia over the following four years, according to a new study. Researchers found that vaccinated adults had a 24% lower risk of dementia compared with those who did not receive the vaccine.

The analysis drew on Medicare data and health records from more than 500,000 adults age 66 and older who were admitted to skilled nursing facilities for either short-term or long-term care. Researchers compared patients who received at least one dose of the recombinant shingles vaccine, known as RZV or Shingrix, with patients who remained unvaccinated. Shingrix was introduced in 2017 and is currently the only shingles vaccine available on the market.

"A lot of previous studies with similar results focused on an older vaccine," said study author Kaley Hayes, an assistant professor at Brown University's School of Public Health. "This study looks at the newest vaccine only in an older, vulnerable adult population who were not up to date with shingles vaccination and are at a very clear clinical point in care: entering a skilled nursing facility."

The results are consistent with several earlier studies involving a previous shingles vaccine that also found an association between shingles vaccination and a reduced risk of dementia.

"It fits into this large puzzle that's just starting to come together that the vaccines are effective at preventing shingles and also appear to have neuroprotective benefits as well," said Hayes, who is also the associate director of pharmacoepidemiology for Brown's Center for Gerontology and Healthcare Research.

Hayes led the study, published in Annals of Internal Medicine , with researchers from Brown, the University of Delaware, the Providence Veterans Affairs Medical Center and other institutions.

The researchers used a technique called target trial emulation to analyze the data. This approach attempts to recreate some of the conditions of a randomized clinical trial in situations where conducting such a trial is not practical.

The study included Medicare claims and electronic health records from patients admitted to more than 5,500 skilled nursing facilities nationwide between 2017 and 2022. Of the 509,926 people included in the analysis, just 8,843 received the shingles vaccine.

Participants had to be eligible for shingles vaccination and could not have previously been diagnosed with dementia.

After four years of follow-up, adults who had received at least one of the two Shingrix doses were substantially less likely to receive a dementia diagnosis. Dementia developed in 18.8% of vaccinated participants, compared with 24.6% of those who were not vaccinated.

title.en: Atomic catalyst unlocks the hidden value of plant waste
title.zh: 原子催化剂释放植物废物的隐藏价值

summary.en: Scientists have created a highly efficient catalyst that breaks down stubborn lignin from plant waste into useful chemicals under relatively mild conditions. By revealing exactly how the catalyst works at the atomic level, the discovery could help turn forestry and agricultural...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Lignin gives plants much of their structural strength and represents the largest renewable source of aromatic chemicals found in nature. It can make up a substantial share (up to 35%) of waste biomass from agriculture and forestry. Yet lignin's complicated molecular structure makes it notoriously difficult to break apart efficiently, which has limited its potential use in sustainable manufacturing.

In a study published in ACS Catalysis , an international team that included Dr. Christopher Parlett, Xinyue Zhou, and Yutao Jiang from the Department of Chemical Engineering developed a highly efficient "single-atom catalyst." The researchers also determined, at the molecular level, how the catalyst breaks the strong chemical bonds that help hold lignin together.

The catalyst contains individual ruthenium atoms embedded within a nitrogen-doped carbon material. By keeping the ruthenium atoms isolated, the design can deliver strong catalytic performance while requiring only very small amounts of metal, improving efficiency compared with conventional systems.

One persistent obstacle in lignin research has been identifying exactly which parts of a catalyst are responsible for breaking the material's unusually strong chemical bonds. Without that information, researchers have had limited guidance for designing more effective catalysts.

The team found that a particular atomic arrangement known as a "Ru-N 4 site" is especially important. These sites activate oxygen molecules and help trigger the breaking of both carbon-oxygen and carbon-carbon bonds within lignin.

Using a combination of laboratory experiments and computational modeling, the researchers were able to reconstruct the process in greater detail. The catalyst first activates oxygen, producing highly reactive species. Those species then attack the lignin structure and split it into smaller molecules.

When tested under optimized conditions, the catalyst converted nearly all of the model lignin compounds and generated high yields of valuable chemical products, including phenol.

The process also works under relatively mild conditions and does not require harsh chemicals. That combination could make the approach useful for developing more sustainable methods of chemical manufacturing.

The researchers went beyond simplified model compounds and tested the catalyst on real lignin collected from several biomass sources. It successfully converted those samples into useful aromatic compounds that could potentially become building blocks for fuels, plastics, and other materials.

The findings provide a more detailed picture of how single-atom catalysts operate during biomass conversion. That understanding could serve as a guide for developing more efficient catalytic systems in the future.

title.en: Tornado tears through French village, leaving dozens hurt and homes ravaged
title.zh: 龙卷风席卷法国村庄，数十人受伤，房屋被毁

summary.en: A tornado struck the village of Pomas in southwestern France, causing widespread damage to hundreds of homes and injuring 39 people, with 15 requiring hospitalization.
summary.zh: 一场龙卷风袭击了法国西南部的波马斯村，摧毁了数百所房屋，造成39人受伤，其中15人被送往医院。

body.en:
A tornado has torn through the village of Pomas in south-west France, injuring 39 people and damaging hundreds of homes.

Authorities said 15 people were taken to hospital and two were in a critical condition. One man said his pregnant wife was injured after their house collapsed on her.

More than 120 emergency workers were deployed to the village south of Carcassonne after winds reaching 117km/h (73mph) tore roofs off houses and damaged an estimated 300 homes on Monday.

"Half the village has been destroyed," said one resident called Pierre, who described the tornado as swirling like a "huge red and yellow chimney".

"There's a huge castle and a third of it is has collapsed - even though these are stones that have stood for 1,000 years," Pierre told Ici Occitanie.

The third stage of the Vuelta a España cycle race, which was taking place in the Aude area of south-western France, had to be cancelled when a hail storm forced the riders to take shelter about 15km from the finish line.

The extreme weather has left about 2,800 homes across 10 villages without electricity, according to officials.

Local sub-prefect Emmanuelle Plantier-Lemarchand told French radio that she was not aware of anyone missing. She lowered the number of victims from 41 to 39, and said 15 of them had been treated in hospital.

"I heard this massive noise... then I saw everything flying around in the air and my roof collapsed over my head," shocked resident Chantal told French radio. "I've got no house left, that's for sure... I was really scared. I thought that's it, this my final hour."

French authorities had issued an orange alert for thunderstorms in large parts of the country's south-west, which have already been hit by power outages and transport disruptions.

Eyewitness footage from the region captured the swirling vortex of the tornado looming in the horizon above houses and trees.

Images from the small village of Pomas, which was the hardest hit, showed uprooted trees, damaged cars and rubble from destroyed homes.

Meanwhile there were flight delays and cancellations at airports in Bordeaux, Marseille, Nice, Toulouse and north of Paris to the north, said Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot.

On average, France experiences several dozen tornadoes per year, according to the country's national weather service Météo-France.

It comes after Europe's summer of unprecedented heatwaves and wildfires, with France's south-west region among the worst affected with an area of 42,000 hectares burnt in one of the largest forest fires since World War Two.
body.zh: 一场龙卷风席卷了法国西南部的波马斯村，造成 39 人受伤，数百所房屋受损。 当局表示，15 人被送往医院，其中两人情况危急。一名男子说，他怀孕的妻子在房子倒塌后受伤。 周一，时速 117 公里（73 英里）的大风掀翻了房屋屋顶，估计有 300 所房屋受损，超过 120 名紧急救援人员被部署到卡尔卡松以南的村庄。 “半个村庄已被摧毁，”一位名叫皮埃尔的居民说，他形容龙卷风像“巨大的红黄色烟囱”一样旋转。 “有一座巨大的城堡，尽管这些石头已经屹立了 1000 年，但它的三分之一已经倒塌了，”皮埃尔告诉 Ici Occitanie。 环西班牙自行车赛第三赛段在法国西南部奥德地区举行，由于冰雹迫使车手们在距终点线约 15 公里处避难，比赛不得不取消。 据官员称，极端天气导致 10 个村庄约 2,800 户家庭断电。 当地副省长埃曼纽尔·普朗蒂埃·勒马尔尚 (Emmanuelle Plantier-Lemarchan) 告诉法国电台，她不知道有人失踪。她将受害者人数从 41 人减少到 39 人，并表示其中 15 人已在医院接受治疗。 震惊的居民尚塔尔告诉法国电台：“我听到巨大的噪音……然后我看到一切都在空中飞舞，我的屋顶倒塌了。” “我已经没有房子了，这是肯定的。” 法国当局已对该国西南部大部分地区发布雷暴橙色警报，这些地区已经遭受停电和交通中断的影响。 该地区的目击者镜头捕捉到龙卷风的漩涡在房屋和树木上方的地平线上若隐若现。 来自受灾最严重的波马斯小村庄的图像显示，树木被连根拔起，汽车受损，房屋被毁，瓦砾遍地。 与此同时，交通部长菲利普·塔巴罗特表示，波尔多、马赛、尼斯、图卢兹以及巴黎北部的机场都出现了航班延误和取消。 据法国国家气象局称，法国平均每年会经历数十次龙卷风。 此前，欧洲夏季遭遇了前所未有的热浪和野火，法国西南部地区是受影响最严重的地区，面积达 42,000 公顷，是第二次世界大战以来最大规模的森林火灾之一。

The Apostle Paul writes that all of creation groans, awaiting redemption from decay and destruction. In moments of natural disaster, we witness this groaning firsthand, a shared suffering that calls for compassion and hope in God's ultimate...
reflection.zh: 法国波马斯村遭受龙卷风袭击的毁灭性力量，提醒我们世界的脆弱。使徒保罗写道，万物都在一同叹息，劳苦，直到如今，等待着救赎脱离败坏的辖制。在自然灾害的时刻，我们亲眼目睹了这种叹息，一种共同的苦难，呼唤着怜悯和对上帝最终复兴的盼望。

title.en: Scientists find hidden “highways” guiding animal evolution
title.zh: 科学家发现指导动物进化的隐藏“高速公路”

summary.en: A sweeping analysis of thousands of animal genomes suggests that chromosomes do not evolve randomly but instead follow a limited number of irreversible “evolutionary highways.” These one-way genetic changes preserve clues to more than 600 million years of animal history and...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A human, an octopus, and a coral may appear to have almost nothing in common, but their chromosomes still contain recognizable fragments inherited from an animal ancestor that lived more than 600 million years ago. Researchers at the University of Vienna have now traced how those ancient genomic pieces were reorganized as animal life diversified.

The study, published in Science Advances , suggests that animal genomes do not evolve through an unlimited number of possible routes. Instead, chromosome changes tend to move along a restricted set of irreversible pathways that the researchers describe as "evolutionary highways." The findings may also provide a valuable foundation for efforts to understand and conserve animal biodiversity.

Every living animal ultimately descends from a common ancestor that existed more than 600 million years ago. Since that time, chromosomes have repeatedly fused, separated, and been rearranged as new animal lineages emerged.

Thousands of animal genomes have now been sequenced, but comparing their long-term evolution has remained difficult. In this study, an international team led by University of Vienna researchers brought thousands of genomes together in a single large-scale comparison.

"Understanding these rules of evolution doesn't just tell us about the past," said Oleg Simakov, a professor at the University of Vienna who co-led the study. "It also lets us ask where genome evolution might go next and enables us to identify key measures for the conservation of animal biodiversity."

Many sequenced genomes remain "drafts." They can reveal which genes an animal possesses without showing exactly where those genes are positioned along its chromosomes. Chromosome-scale assemblies provide much more detail by arranging genes in their proper order across complete chromosomes. Producing these assemblies is considerably more difficult, and only recently have enough species been analyzed at this level to make a broad comparison across the animal kingdom possible.

The researchers examined more than 5,800 publicly available chromosome-scale genomes representing 4,454 species from 19 animal phyla. According to the team, this is the largest comparison of its kind across the animal tree of life.

To organize such a vast amount of information, the scientists created a framework called evolutionary genome topology. It places the enormous variety of animal genome structures onto a single map.

That map revealed an important pattern. Genome architecture does not appear to change randomly. Instead, animal lineages tend to move along "evolutionary highways." Evidence from hundreds of living species shows that different groups traveled along these routes or departed from them at different times and at different rates.

title.en: NASA finds Earth microbes could survive on the Moon
title.zh: NASA发现地球微生物可以在月球上生存

summary.en: NASA scientists found that microbes brought by astronauts could survive in cold, shadowed niches around the Moon’s South Pole, potentially complicating future searches for pristine lunar chemistry. Some refuges may be no larger than a footprint, while one hardy fungus could even...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
NASA scientists say some microbes carried into space by human explorers may be able to survive in sheltered, shadowed areas near the Moon's South Pole.

The findings, published on Aug. 19, 2026, in Science Advances , underscore the importance of understanding how long Earth microbes can persist in extreme lunar environments. As people establish a more permanent presence on the Moon, contamination from astronauts could make it harder for scientists to separate ancient lunar chemistry from material introduced by humans. Researchers say the same issue will matter when missions eventually search for signs of life on Mars.

"Humans are natural explorers, and with them come their voices, their memories … and their microbes," said Prabal Saxena, a planetary scientist who led the study from NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. "For some scientists, myself included, that reality can be unsettling. But it also creates an opportunity to turn an imperfect situation into a useful experiment."

Humans inevitably carry microbes with them. On average, about 1 million bacteria live on every patch of skin roughly the size of a pencil eraser. Some of these organisms can escape from spacesuits and habitats into the surrounding environment.

That creates a challenge for scientists hoping to study chemical evidence connected to the Moon's ancient geology or possible biology. At the same time, the researchers argue that the Moon could serve as a valuable natural laboratory. Carefully monitored shadowed regions near the South Pole could allow scientists to test the real limits of microbial survival under conditions that are extremely difficult to reproduce on Earth.

Before those experiments can begin, however, researchers need to establish a clear baseline showing what contaminants humans introduce.

"We need to understand what was there before us, because when we go to Mars to search for signs of life beyond our planet, we will want to make sure it's not stuff we brought," said Andrew Needham, a NASA Goddard-based paper co-author who is an Artemis contamination-control scientist for lunar samples.

Even rigorous sterilization cannot eliminate every hardy organism. One example is Aspergillus niger , a fungus that commonly grows in warm, humid environments such as bathrooms and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems.

Astronauts have collected samples of the fungus aboard the International Space Station, and previous experiments have shown that it can also survive outside the station. Aspergillus niger was one of five microbes examined in the new study because of its demonstrated resilience in spaceflight conditions.

Scientists were surprised that microbes like these could endure exposure on the exterior of the space station....
body.zh: 美国宇航局科学家表示，一些被人类探险家带入太空的微生物可能能够在月球南极附近受庇护的阴影区域生存。 该研究结果于 2026 年 8 月 19 日发表在《科学进展》杂志上，强调了了解地球微生物在月球极端环境中能够存活多久的重要性。随着人们在月球上建立更永久的存在，宇航员的污染可能会使科学家更难将古代月球化学物质与人类引入的物质分开。研究人员表示，当任务最终在火星上寻找生命迹象时，同样的问题也很重要。 “人类是天生的探险家，随之而来的是他们的声音、他们的记忆......以及他们的微生物，”领导这项研究的行星科学家普拉巴尔·萨克塞纳（Prabal Saxena）说，他来自马里兰州格林贝尔特的美国宇航局戈达德太空飞行中心。 “对于包括我在内的一些科学家来说，现实可能会令人不安。但它也创造了一个机会，可以将不完美的情况变成有用的实验。” 人类不可避免地携带微生物。平均而言，每一块橡皮大小的皮肤上都生活着大约 100 万个细菌。其中一些生物体可以从宇航服和栖息地逃逸到周围环境中。 这给希望研究与月球古代地质或可能的生物学有关的化学证据的科学家带来了挑战。与此同时，研究人员认为月球可以作为一个有价值的天然实验室。仔细监测南极附近的阴影区域可以让科学家测试微生物在地球上极难繁殖的条件下生存的真正极限。 然而，在这些实验开始之前，研究人员需要建立一个明确的基线，显示人类引入了哪些污染物。 “我们需要了解在我们之前存在的东西，因为当我们前往火星寻找地球以外的生命迹象时，我们需要确保它不是我们带来的东西，”美国宇航局戈达德论文合著者、月球样本阿耳忒弥斯污染控制科学家安德鲁·尼达姆(Andrew Needham)说。 即使严格的灭菌也不能消灭所有顽强的生物。一个例子是黑曲霉，这是一种通常生长在温暖、潮湿的环境中的真菌，例如浴室和供暖、通风和空调系统。 宇航员在国际空间站上收集了这种真菌的样本，之前的实验表明它也可以在空间站外生存。黑曲霉是这项新研究中检查的五种微生物之一，因为它在太空飞行条件下表现出恢复能力。 科学家们对这样的微生物能够忍受暴露在空间站外部感到惊讶......

title.en: Moon set to turn red as rare partial lunar eclipse graces UK skies
title.zh: 罕见的月偏食照亮英国天空，月亮将变成红色

summary.en: There will be a partial lunar eclipse in the UK on 28 August, and may cause the Moon appear reddish in colour.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Skywatchers across the UK could have the chance to see a stunning partial lunar eclipse later this week as the Sun, Earth, and Moon line up in the night sky.

Lunar eclipses occur when the Moon is full which will take place in the early hours of 28 August. It may cause the full Moon - nicknamed the Sturgeon Moon - to take on an eerie reddish glow.

It comes just weeks after the UK experienced its most dramatic partial solar eclipse in nearly 30 years.

Adding to the spectacle, its position in the sky will be low on the horizon, causing a phenomenon known as the Moon illusion. This makes the Moon appear bigger and more dramatic than usual.

The partial eclipse will begin at 03:33 BST in London, when the Moon enters Earth's darkest shadow.

It will reach its maximum at 05:12 BST, when around 90% of the Moon will be within the umbra.

By this point the Moon will be very low in the south-western sky, causing something known as the Moon illusion .

This is a term for when the Moon appears much larger than it is based on its position in the sky - an effect caused by the way our brains process visual information.

The effect is particularly noticeable during a moonrise or moonset, when the lunar disc is seen alongside familiar objects on the ground.

A lunar eclipse happens when the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon, causing the Moon to temporarily move into the Earth's shadow.

During a partial eclipse, only part of the Moon enters the darkest section of that shadow, known as the umbra.

Sunlight passing through the Earth's atmosphere is scattered, with shorter blue wavelengths scattering more easily, while more of the longer wavelength red light reach the Moon.

These wavelengths are then reflected back towards Earth, giving the eclipsed Moon its reddish colour.

For the best chance of seeing the eclipse, astronomers recommend finding a high location with an unobstructed view towards the south-western horizon.

Viewing conditions are expected to vary considerably across the UK during the early hours of Friday morning.

With low pressure in charge, cloud and heavy showers are likely to affect some parts of the country, while other areas remain clear.

Currently, the best viewing conditions are expected across central and eastern parts of England and Wales. However, even here, the cloud cover could change a lot from one hour to the next and is very hard to forecast accurately.

You can check the latest hour-by-hour forecast where you are online or via the BBC Weather app.
body.zh: 本周晚些时候，当太阳、地球和月亮在夜空中排成一行时，英国各地的天文爱好者可能有机会看到令人惊叹的月偏食。 月食发生在 8 月 28 日凌晨满月时。它可能会导致满月（绰号“鲟鱼月”）呈现出怪异的红色光芒。 就在几周前，英国经历了近 30 年来最剧烈的日偏食。 更糟糕的是，它在天空中的位置将低于地平线，从而导致一种称为月亮错觉的现象。这使得月亮看起来比平时更大、更引人注目。 日偏食将于英国夏令时 03:33 在伦敦开始，届时月球将进入地球最暗的阴影。 它将在英国夏令时 05:12 达到最大值，届时大约 90% 的月球将位于本影内。 此时，月亮将位于西南天空中很低的位置，从而造成所谓的月亮错觉。 这是一个术语，指的是当月球看起来比它在天空中的位置大得多时，这是由我们的大脑处理视觉信息的方式引起的。 这种效应在月出或月落期间尤其明显，此时月盘与地面上熟悉的物体并排出现。 当地球经过太阳和月球之间时，就会发生月食，导致月球暂时移入地球的阴影中。 在日偏食期间，只有月球的一部分进入阴影最暗的部分，即本影。 穿过地球大气层的阳光会被散射，波长较短的蓝色光更容易散射，而更多波长较长的红光到达月球。 然后这些波长被反射回地球，使月食呈现出微红色。 为了获得观看日食的最佳机会，天文学家建议寻找一个可以一览无余地看到西南地平线的高处。 预计周五凌晨英国各地的观看情况会有很大差异。 由于低压，云和大阵雨可能会影响该国的部分地区，而其他地区则保持晴朗。 目前，英格兰和威尔士中部和东部地区的观看条件预计最佳。然而，即使在这里，云量在一小时与下一小时之间也可能发生很大变化，并且很难准确预测。 您可以在线或通过 BBC 天气应用程序查看最新的每小时天气预报。

title.en: Depression may shut down the brain’s ability to make new neurons
title.zh: 抑郁症可能会关闭大脑产生新神经元的能力

summary.en: A major study found that adults with depression show disrupted production of new neurons in the hippocampus, potentially weakening the brain’s ability to separate new experiences from painful memories. The researchers also identified broad molecular changes that could open the...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科学栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Most of the brain's roughly 100 billion neurons are produced before birth. However, the small number of new neurons that continue to form in the adult hippocampus may play an important role in protecting against depression, according to new research from Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons.

The findings provide the first evidence that neurogenesis, the process of producing new neurons, stalls in the brains of adults with major depressive disorder. Researchers also identified molecular programs involved in controlling this process, offering potential clues for developing new treatments.

"Historically, depression was thought to be a disease of neurotransmitter deficiency, especially serotonin, but we now think that depression stems from multiple issues that affect our neurons' ability to adapt to stress and changing environments," says Maura Dupont, professor of psychiatry, who led the research.

"Without the ability to create new neurons, people with depression may not have the resilience to effectively adapt to the environment."

The researchers focused on the hippocampus, a brain region that plays a major role in episodic memory and emotional responses to the environment. It is also one of the few areas of the adult brain that continues to generate new neurons.

Although the hippocampus is not the only brain region involved in depression, its influence over both memory and emotion has made it an important area of study. Researchers believe changes there may contribute to the tendency of people with depression to interpret experiences more negatively.

"The hippocampus is important for our ability to distinguish between similar but different memories and separate the emotional connotation of past memories and current events," Dupont says.

This ability is known as pattern separation. When it becomes impaired, individual memories and the emotions attached to them may become less distinct, allowing separate experiences to blend together.

"You may be out with a friend for lunch, but she's tired and doesn't talk much. With intact pattern separation, you remember this as a unique event. With impaired pattern separation, it becomes mixed with previous memories of feeling rejected, leading you to think, 'They're upset with me'," Dupont explains. "And I see this a lot in my patients, where they can only retrieve negative information from their memories."

Research in mice has shown that adult neurogenesis is necessary for pattern separation. A recent study involving patients with brain tumors, in whom neurogenesis was eliminated by radiation therapy directed at the hippocampus, suggests that the same relationship may exist in humans.

body.zh: 大脑大约 1000 亿个神经元中的大部分是在出生前产生的。然而，根据哥伦比亚大学瓦格洛斯内科医生和外科医生学院的最新研究，成人海马体中继续形成的少量新神经元可能在预防抑郁症方面发挥重要作用。 这些发现提供了第一个证据，表明神经发生（产生新神经元的过程）在患有重度抑郁症的成年人的大脑中停滞。研究人员还确定了参与控制这一过程的分子程序，为开发新疗法提供了潜在线索。 “从历史上看，抑郁症被认为是一种神经递质缺乏的疾病，尤其是血清素缺乏，但我们现在认为抑郁症源于影响我们的神经元适应压力和不断变化的环境的能力的多种问题，”领导这项研究的精神病学教授莫拉·杜邦说。 “如果没有产生新神经元的能力，抑郁症患者可能没有有效适应环境的能力。” 研究人员重点研究了海马体，这是一个在情景记忆和对环境的情绪反应中发挥重要作用的大脑区域。它也是成人大脑中持续产生新神经元的少数区域之一。 虽然海马体不是唯一与抑郁有关的大脑区域，但它对记忆和情绪的影响使其成为一个重要的研究领域。研究人员认为，那里的变化可能会导致抑郁症患者倾向于更消极地解释经历。 杜邦说：“海马体对于我们区分相似但不同的记忆以及区分过去记忆和当前事件的情感内涵的能力非常重要。” 这种能力称为模式分离。当它受到损害时，个人记忆和与之相关的情感可能会变得不那么清晰，从而使不同的经历能够融合在一起。 “你可能和朋友出去吃午饭，但她很累，话不多。如果模式分离完整，你会记得这是一个独特的事件。如果模式分离受损，它会与之前被拒绝的记忆混合在一起，导致你思考，‘他们对我感到不安’，”杜邦解释道。 “我在我的病人身上经常看到这种情况，他们只能从记忆中检索负面信息。” 对小鼠的研究表明，成年神经发生对于模式分离是必要的。最近一项涉及脑肿瘤患者的研究表明，在人类中也可能存在同样的关系，这些患者的神经发生通过针对海马体的放射治疗而被消除。 “需要强调的是，我们还不知道完整的机制，特别是......

title.en: Goat sanctuary purchases 16.9 acres of more land
title.zh: 山羊收容所购买更多土地

summary.en: Buttercups Sanctuary for Goats has purchased an additional 16.9 acres of land, which will allow them to house up to 160 goats. Sanctuary director Matt Huggins described the purchase as the 'most significant step since the charity's foundation,' fulfilling a long-held dream.
summary.zh: 黄油杯山羊收容所（Buttercups Sanctuary for Goats）购买了额外的16.9英亩土地，这将使他们能够容纳多达160只山羊。收容所主管马特·哈金斯（Matt Huggins）称此次收购是“自慈善机构成立以来最重要的举措”，实现了长久以来的梦想。

body.en:
A goat sanctuary in Kent has purchased an additional 16.9 acres of land, which it said would enable it to house up to 160 goats.

Buttercups Sanctuary for Goats in Boughton Monchelsea said that the new plot of land was close to where it was currently situated and would provide "long-lasting results for both our adorable residents and the wider, beautiful countryside".

Matt Huggins said that it was the "most significant step since the charity's foundation".

"It's been something we've all been dreaming of for a long, long time, and we're all very excited to get going," Huggins added.

According to the sanctuary, the purchased plot of land had historically been used for agriculture and will enable it to rescue more goats and double its on-site capacity.

It said a lot of work would need to be carried out on the land despite being a "blank canvas", but new goats are expected to begin living there by spring 2027.

Huggins added that its long-term vision included solar panels, wind turbines and habitat networks for the wildlife, which he expected would take years to be fully completed.

"There's a long road ahead, and we are going to need the help of our supporters to make it a final reality, but we've taken the first major step," he said.

body.zh: 肯特郡的一个山羊保护区额外购买了 16.9 英亩的土地，据称这可以容纳多达 160 只山羊。 鲍顿蒙切尔西的毛茛山羊保护区表示，新的土地靠近目前所在的位置，并将“为我们可爱的居民和更广阔、美丽的乡村提供持久的成果”。 马特·哈金斯表示，这是“自该慈善机构成立以来最重要的一步”。 哈金斯补充道：“这是我们长期以来一直梦想的事情，我们都非常兴奋能够开始。” 据该保护区称，所购买的土地历来用于农业，这将使其能够拯救更多的山羊并将其现场容量增加一倍。 报告称，尽管这片土地是一块“空白画布”，但仍需要进行大量工作，但预计到 2027 年春季，新山羊将开始在那里生活。 哈金斯补充说，其长期愿景包括太阳能电池板、风力涡轮机和野生动物栖息地网络，他预计这需要数年时间才能完全完成。 他说：“前面的路还很长，我们需要支持者的帮助才能使其成为最终现实，但我们已经迈出了重要的第一步。” 在 Facebook（外部）、X（外部）和 Instagram（外部）上关注 BBC Kent。将您的故事创意发送至东南部今天@bbc.co.uk、外部或通过 WhatsApp 联系我们 08081 002250。

summary.zh: 这是一则来自科技栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Fashionistas of a certain age no doubt remember the late designer Stephen Sprouse , who gave Blondie's Debbie Harry her distinctive Bowery punk style. Sprouse's first collections in the mid-1980s made a major splash, melding graffiti prints, a playful '60s aesthetic, and bright Day-Glo colors that won admirers such as Andy Warhol. Several examples of Sprouse's work are preserved in the textiles collection of the Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields, where conservationists are trying to learn more about the phosphorescent and fluorescent pigments the designer used in his creations in order to keep the colors from dulling over time. They described recent advances in that research at a meeting of the American Chemical Society (ACS) held this week in Chicago. Scientists began describing minerals that glowed in the dark as phosphors in the Middle Ages. Typically such materials take on a charge when exposed to light, storing the absorbed energy and releasing it gradually as re-emitted light. Henri Becquerel discovered radioactive decay in 1896 because of his work with phosphorescent uranium salts: He left the salts in a closed drawer with photographic plates, which fogged up even without a light source. DayGlo paints and similar materials exploit the related phenomenon of fluorescence. DayGlo pigments fluoresce in daylight by essentially converting UV light into visible light to produce brighter, more vibrant colors. Read full article Comments
body.zh: 某个年龄段的时尚达人无疑还记得已故设计师 Stephen Sprouse，他为 Blondie 的 Debbie Harry 赋予了独特的 Bowery 朋克风格。 Sprouse 在 20 世纪 80 年代中期推出的首个系列引起了巨大轰动，融合了涂鸦印花、俏皮的 60 年代美学以及明亮的 Day-Glo 色彩，赢得了安迪·沃霍尔 (Andy Warhol) 等崇拜者的青睐。纽菲尔德印第安纳波利斯艺术博物馆的纺织品收藏中保存了斯普罗斯作品的几个例子，那里的自然资源保护主义者正在尝试更多地了解设计师在他的创作中使用的磷光和荧光颜料，以防止颜色随着时间的推移而变暗。他们在本周于芝加哥举行的美国化学会 (ACS) 会议上描述了该研究的最新进展。中世纪时，科学家们开始将在黑暗中发光的矿物质描述为磷光体。通常，此类材料在暴露于光时会带电，存储吸收的能量并以重新发射的光的形式逐渐释放能量。 1896 年，亨利·贝克勒尔 (Henri Becquerel) 在研究磷光铀盐时发现了放射性衰变：他将盐放在一个装有照相底片的封闭抽屉中，即使没有光源，底片也会起雾。 DayGlo 涂料和类似材料利用了相关的荧光现象。 DayGlo 颜料在日光下发出荧光，本质上是将紫外线转化为可见光，从而产生更明亮、更鲜艳的颜色。阅读全文 评论

title.en: Google's anti-nausea Motion Assist dots finally rolling out on Android
title.zh: 谷歌的抗恶心运动辅助点终于在Android上推出

summary.en: It's currently only appearing on Pixels running Android 17.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自科技栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Some people are cursed with motion sickness, which can make it impossible to read or use a phone in a moving vehicle without suffering waves of nausea. There's a surprisingly simple trick that can make smartphones usable in such situations. Apple deployed it on the iPhone a couple of years ago, and now Google's own version is finally coming (slowly) to Android. Motion sickness is caused by a disagreement between what your inner ear senses and what your eyes see. If you're looking at a book or a screen while in a car, the sensory mismatch can lead to a pretty unpleasant time. As part of iOS 18 in 2024, Apple released a feature called Motion Cues that places a network of moving dots on the screen to alleviate motion sickness, and it seems to work surprisingly well. Google's version is similar, but it's called Motion Assist. Google began testing Motion Assist back in 2024, but it never expanded beyond an internal test until now. Android Authority reports Motion Assist is appearing on Pixel phones running Android 17, but there's no app or update you can install to get the feature—it's being delivered by Play Services as part of a staged rollout. Read full article Comments
body.zh: 有些人患有晕车症，在行驶的车辆中阅读或使用手机时会感到一阵阵恶心。有一个令人惊讶的简单技巧可以使智能手机在这种情况下可用。几年前，苹果公司在 iPhone 上部署了它，现在谷歌自己的版本终于（缓慢地）登陆 Android 了。晕动病是由于内耳感觉与眼睛看到的不一致引起的。如果你在车里看书或看屏幕，感官上的不匹配可能会导致一段非常不愉快的时光。作为 2024 年 iOS 18 的一部分，苹果发布了一项名为 Motion Cues 的功能，该功能在屏幕上放置移动点网络来缓解晕动病，而且效果似乎出奇的好。谷歌的版本类似，但它被称为Motion Assist。谷歌早在 2024 年就开始测试 Motion Assist，但直到现在才扩展到内部测试之外。 Android Authority 报告称，Motion Assist 出现在运行 Android 17 的 Pixel 手机上，但您无法安装任何应用程序或更新来获取该功能，该功能由 Play Services 作为分阶段推出的一部分提供。阅读全文 评论

title.en: Two unvaccinated people die from measles in Pennsylvania, officials confirm
